FlyBot is three plugins on top of a pinned [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot) core for
[DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness):

- **`@flybot/tree`** — a recursive Bot tree that splits a request, delegates level by level, and combines answers on the way back up.
- **`@flybot/social`** — connect your Bots as friends with other homes and chat through a self-hosted [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server, with owner approvals.
- **`@flybot/timeline`** (optional, off by default) — see where your team's time goes: swimlanes per Bot, who waits on whom, and how busy each Bot is.

## Features

### Tree plugin (`@flybot/tree`)

Turns your Bots into one recursive tree that splits a request into parts, sends each part down a level, and combines the answers on the way back up.

![Tree plugin: Chief splits a Hangzhou trip across Travel, Food, and Budget](docs/images/demo-tree.gif)

*Demo: Chief starts alone in the sidebar, creates the child Bots Travel, Food and Budget, hands each one a part, and then combines their answers into one plan. Some waiting is sped up.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-tree.mp4)

- **One root.** The tree's root is the Main Bot (Chief); no new bot is created for it. A separate `Root` bot is created only if the team has Bots but no Main Bot. Every other local Bot joins the tree, including one made with `create_bot` or the Bot list, under the same limits as `create_child_bot`. The tree organizes itself by role: a new Bot goes into the group that matches its role, and when a level is full (and once a day) related Bots are grouped under a suitable existing lead or a new lead with a clear role, such as "FlyBot Lead" for dev / test / repo Bots or "Life Lead" for cooking / shopping. Duplicate Bots are merged and long-idle ones archived after 30 days; nothing is deleted. Every change is logged, the sidebar shows what the last reorganization did, and one click undoes it.
- **Children on demand.** Any tree Bot (not only the Main/root) calls `create_child_bot(name, role_description)` to make a child directly under *itself*; the tool takes no parent argument. Calls are handled one at a time per parent, so parallel calls never go over the limits or create two siblings with the same name. The rules:
  - names are 1–40 characters, and duplicate sibling names are rejected (case and spaces ignored);
  - depth is at most 5 (the root counts as 1), with at most 8 children per Bot (set in `limits.json` or the plugin config);
  - a new child is usable only by its creator's owner; sharing it still needs an independent per-Bot grant (default deny — no publish).
- **Level-by-level delegation.** Each Bot sees only its direct children (`list_children()`), never deeper levels.
  - A Bot with children acts as coordinator: it splits the task, sends each part to the child whose scope fits, waits, and combines the answers for its parent.
  - A Bot with no children does the work itself.
- **Message rules** (the `tree` send policy):
  - a tree Bot may message its parent, its direct children, and remote (friends') Bots (the tree never blocks remote messages; the social plugin decides);
  - the root may also message any local Bot;
  - local Bots outside the tree may message only the root;
  - `stopped` and `report` notices are never blocked, so Chief can always stop any Bot.
- **Reparenting.** When a Bot is deleted, its children move up to its parent. The parent and every moved subtree get a fresh prompt and trace, and no child is dropped. If the parent is then over `maxChildren`, its children are regrouped by role the same way.
- **Trace line.** When a tree Bot answers its *parent*, it starts the answer with its path, e.g. `Chief → Work → Dev`. Replies to you or to a friend's Bot never include it, and the root never adds one.
- **Your prompts are kept.** The plugin adds its rules in a marked block inside each Bot's system prompt and replaces only that block, so text you wrote yourself is never overwritten.
- **Sidebar.** The Bot list is drawn as one expandable tree with Chief on top. Retired, archived and other Main Bots are shown directly under Chief, with a tag for archived, idle or (rarely) outside-the-tree Bots; every other Bot is drawn where the tree has it.

Install (needs the core, `path:/core`):

```bash
npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/tree"
```

# flybot-social Every local Bot can chat with friends' Bots on a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server. The plugin talks to a Bot Social server that you self-host; see the Bot Social README for install and configuration. Host: `index.js`; browser: `client.js`. Design: see "Social design: homes and members" in the root README. - **Server in Settings** (#337): Settings → **Bot Social** shows the server, where it comes from and the connection, and switches to another server without a restart (`https://`, or `http://localhost`; `/v1/platform` is read first and its features shown). The choice is kept in `flybot-social-server.json` beside the credentials; `config.server` stays the default. A server is an identity: each has its own credentials file (the previous one is kept, never deleted), settings, and per-Bot identities and grants, and switching back restores them. - **One-click onboarding**: on first start, `POST /v1/onboard/flybot` creates the owner, the home identity (`@.home`), and a connector token in one call; credentials go to `credentialsPath` (default `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-social.json`, mode 600). If `@.home` is taken, onboarding retries `Name2`, `Name3`, … so a second install can start without editing YAML. Sidebar **+** → **Copy my handle** copies the connected handle. If start still fails, it shows **Social is not running:** with the reason instead of the host's `Unknown FlyBot endpoint` message. The same failure is written to Settings → Feedback. - **Members**: a local Bot becomes `@.` (`add_home_member`) when it is invited, when it joins an invite, or at face-to-face join, stored as field `social.member`. There is no published flag: access is a per-Bot **grant** (Sharing → Copy invite link → accept). Default deny, Chief included. Deleted Bots are revoked on `bot.removed`. Ungranted Bots are not registered at start and are not polled. **Face-to-face join** of my own Bot is an implicit room-scoped grant: if it has no identity yet, the plugin registers it room-only (`social.member.roomOnly`). That identity does not appear in friends' `list_remote_bots`, and `reach()` still denies anything outside the room. When you leave the last face room or the room closes, the plugin revokes it (`remove_home_member`). A failed join that created a new room-only identity is revoked too. A later person-grant reuses the handle and drops `roomOnly`. **Manage access** on the Bot lists who has it and **Revoke**. - **Thinking status** (#297): a friend's Bot shows `Name is thinking…` above the composer in its chat and in a face-to-face room while it works, through Bot Social's ephemeral `presence` signal (`set_presence` / `list_presence`; handle, name and state only). Sent only for turns that answer a friend or run in an open room; polled only while such a chat is on screen; nothing happens against a Bot Social that does not list `presence`. Option `presence: false` turns it off. - **Remote roster**: `list_remote_bots` → friends' Bots published into the main Bot list (globe mark). Each row uses the published `avatar` / `color` when the server sends them, else a handle-seeded look. Sidebar section `flybot.sidebar.section#social` keeps **N to approve**, + panels, and **Past rooms**. `@` rows via `flybot.composer.mention#social`. Remote Bots never enter `bot.list()`. **Remove this Bot** declines that grant (`decline_bot_grant`) so it leaves the owner's Manage access; an older server hides it locally.

Install (needs the core, `path:/core`): ```bash npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/tree" ``` ### Social plugin (`@flybot/social`) Every local Bot can chat with friends' Bots through a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server that **you self-host**. Invites are per Bot; what your Bots send on their own can wait for your approval; everything a friend's Bot writes arrives fenced as untrusted text. ![Social plugin: invite a friend, message their Bot, approve the held reply, and see it arrive](docs/images/demo-social.gif) *Demo: one owner invites a friend to their Chief from **Sharing**; the friend pastes the link in **Add friend** (the link is hidden in the video) and messages that Chief. The Chief's reply waits in the owner's chat with an **Approve** card, and after **Approve** it arrives in the friend's chat. Some waiting is sped up.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-social.mp4) - **One-click onboarding.** On first start with a `server` configured, FlyBot calls `POST /v1/onboard/flybot`, creates your home (`@.home`), and stores credentials in `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-social.json` (mode 600). - **Members.** Access is a per-Bot **grant** (default deny, Chief included). A local Bot becomes `@.` on the server when you invite someone to that Bot, when it joins an invite, or when you bring it into a face-to-face room. The sidebar lists only Bots granted to you. **Manage access** on a Bot shows who has it and **Revoke**. Deleted Bots are revoked. Ungranted Bots have no outside identity: friends cannot reach them and they cannot message friends. - **Connectors (GitHub, Composio).** Settings → **Connectors** connects an account once; it is **on for every one of your Bots**, new and existing, on every turn: in its own chat, in group chats, on scheduled tasks, in sub-agents, and when a friend uses a Bot you shared. A friend's own Bot never gets it. You can turn a Bot's connector off (**Choose Bots**, or the **Connectors** card in the Bot's settings). Bots use the GitHub connector first and the saved token in the shell only as a fallback (for example `git push`). Disconnecting resets every Bot's choices. - **Friends in the Bot list.** A friend's Bot sits in the same sidebar list as yours, with a small globe after the name. Face-to-face rooms sit there too, with a people mark; ended ones fold under **Past rooms**. Click a row to open a normal chat. Sidebar **+** → **Add friend** (paste a handle, invite link or code), **Face-to-face room**, and **Copy my handle**. On a local Bot: right-click / settings **Sharing** → **Copy invite link for **, then **Copy link** / **Copy with instructions** / **New link** (the same control as **Add friend** → **Invite a friend**); **People with access** lists who has it and **Revoke**. Each person row there also has **Auto-send** for that Bot → that person (default off); **Auto-send from now on** on a held reply turns on that same switch. - **Face-to-face rooms.** Sidebar **+** → **Face-to-face room**: pick one or more of your Bots, enter the **same 6-digit number** as your friend (about 10 minutes), wait, then **Enter chat** (or **Leave**). No prior friendship and no preview of the other home's other Bots. Your typed lines are sent as you (when the server supports `typed_by_owner`); `@Name` / the picker label / a handle asks that Bot; `@all` asks everyone. A plain line with no `@` is answered by the one Bot it is for (each Bot passes silently unless the line fits it; the Bot that spoke last gets follow-ups; the first Bot answers if all pass); a line to everyone ("introduce yourselves", "你们…") may get one answer from each. Bot-written room lines still go through Approve unless face **Auto-send** is on (open room overview; default off). - **Typed by the owner · mentions · thinking.** Against a Bot Social that lists these under `GET /v1/platform` `features`: your typed friend-DM and face lines can be stamped `typed_by_owner` so the other home draws them as you; face sends may carry an explicit `mentions` handle list; a quiet `Name is thinking…` line appears above the composer while a Bot of another home works in a friend DM or a face-to-face room (ephemeral `presence`; DM path [#360](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/pull/360) / [#332](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/issues/332)). Older servers simply omit what they do not support. - **Approvals.** Inbound messages from a friend arrive immediately (fenced as untrusted). Outbound replies may wait in the open chat (badge + Approve / Reject) until you decide, unless Auto-send is on for that Bot and person (the Bot's **Sharing** → **People with access**) or for the face room. FlyBot also holds a Bot's own send behind an approval card; files are always held. - **Tools.** Every local Bot gets `list_friend_bots` and `message_friend_bot` (with optional file attachments). ![Face-to-face room: two homes join with the same 6-digit number and chat with their Bots](docs/images/demo-face.gif) *Demo: each home picks its Bots in **+** → **Face-to-face room** and types the same 6-digit number, then **Enter chat**. A plain line is answered by Bots in the room; **@Planner** is answered by that Bot alone. Auto-send was on in this demo so Bot lines post without a hold. Some waiting is sped up.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-face.mp4) The social plugin stays idle until you point it at a Bot Social server (see [Quick Start](#quick-start) below). ### Timeline plugin (`@flybot/timeline`) **Optional and off by default.** Installing the package does not show anything or record anything; you turn it on (see below). When on, it shows where the time goes across your local Bot team, from a **Timeline** row under the Bot list. It reads the core's activity feed and keeps a capped trace (about 3000 spans or 24 hours); it stores ids, times and names only, never message text, tool arguments or output. - **Swimlanes.** One lane for you, one per Bot, one per group (a round is drawn as round brackets). Each turn is a bar with its tool calls inside; arrows are messages (dashed requests, solid replies) with the time to the answer, and an open request shows how long it has been waiting. - **Who waits on whom.** A map of the requests between Bots with median wait per edge, plus a table with the slowest and still-unanswered ones. - **Utilization.** Per Bot: model time, tool time and time with no running turn. - **Honest numbers.** Times are when a message reached the other Bot's log, not when it was read. "No running turn" is not "waiting". "Model" time is turn time outside tool calls, not a measured model latency. Install (needs the core), then turn it on: ```bash npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/timeline" ``` ```yaml # profile cordis.patch.yml - id: flybot-timeline config: enabled: true # starts the recorder and the endpoint sidebarSection: true # shows the Timeline row (browser side) ``` Without `enabled: true` it records nothing and keeps no files; without `sidebarSection: true` no row is drawn. ## Quick Start ### 1. Prerequisites - **Node.js 22.19+** and **pnpm** (`npm install -g pnpm`, or `corepack enable`). - **Git**, to install from GitHub. - An API key for at least one model provider (for example DeepSeek: see [Set a DeepSeek API key](docs/deepseek-api-key.md)). ### 2. Install FlyBot (core + plugins) ```sh npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/core" npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/social" npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/tree" ``` The first line is the FlyBot core (package `ds-bot`). The plugins are optional but recommended. `@flybot/timeline` is off by default; see [its section](#timeline-plugin-flybottimeline) to add and turn it on. On DSH Desktop: **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste one of the `github:` addresses above, then **Install** and **Enable now**. ### 3. Run the web app ```sh npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 web --port 3080 ``` Open the printed `http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=…` link. The first time you open Chief, pick a model (or open **Models and providers…**). A picture reaches a model that cannot read images as text: FlyBot reads it with one that can, and names the file on disk when no model can (see [Models](core/README.md#models)). To run FlyBot on a Linux server that stays on, one instance per person, use the container: [Run FlyBot in Docker](docs/docker.md). ### 4. Self-host Bot Social (for friends' Bots) `@flybot/social` needs a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server. It does not ship one. Deploy Bot Social yourself (see its README), then set a public base URL so invite links work: ```sh # example only — use your own host export PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://your-server.example.com export PORT=8787 # start Bot Social as documented in https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social ``` Point FlyBot at that server in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (or `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`), then **restart** DSH: ```yaml - id: flybot-social config: server: https://your-server.example.com # e.g. https://47-80-69-220.sslip.io displayName: Your Name ``` On first start FlyBot calls `POST /v1/onboard/flybot`, registers your home (`@.home`), and stores credentials in `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-social.json` (mode 600). No Bot is shared until you grant it. If that home handle is already taken, FlyBot retries a suffixed name (`Your Name2`, …). Sidebar **+** → **Copy my handle** copies the connected handle. If Social failed to start, the UI shows **Social is not running:** with the reason (also under Settings → Feedback). **Change the server later** without editing YAML: Settings → **Bot Social** shows the server and its connection status, **Change server** checks the new address (`https://`, or `http://localhost` for development; FlyBot reads `/v1/platform` and shows its features) and, after a clear warning, switches without a restart. A new server is a **new identity**: your friends and sharing stay on the old server, your old credentials file is kept as a backup and never deleted, and switching back restores them. The `cordis.patch.yml` value stays the default. **Share one Bot:** that Bot's settings → **Sharing** → **Copy invite link for ** (or **+** → **Add friend** → **Invite a friend**); send the link. Your friend opens sidebar **+** → **Add friend**, pastes the link or code, and accepts — that grant covers **only** that Bot. **People with access** lists who has it; **Revoke** removes them. **Chat:** click the friend's Bot in the sidebar. Their messages arrive at once. What your Bots send back waits in that chat (Approve / Reject) unless **Auto-send** is on for that Bot and that friend (your Bot's **Sharing** → **People with access**, or **Auto-send my Bots' replies to …** on the friend's Bot settings for all your Bots; default off). Look for the **to approve** badge if they see no reply. **Face-to-face:** sidebar **+** → **Face-to-face room** → pick your Bot(s) → enter the **same 6-digit number** within about 10 minutes → **Enter chat**. Friendship is not required. Face **Auto-send** is the checkbox on the open room overview (default off). This is the FlyBot path. Bot Social's separate “tell Grok Bot: set me up following `https://…/setup`” flow is for Grok Bot MCP clients, not for FlyBot. Without a `server`, the social plugin stays idle by design. Tree works without Bot Social. ## Built on FlyBot keeps the upstream DS Bot core byte-identical (`ds-bot/`, pinned in `ds-bot.pin.json`), applies a short FlyBot patch series (`patches/` → `core/`), then adds the plugins under `plugins/`. See [#34](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/issues/34). The web UI (header, About, settings, update popups) says FlyBot; the npm package keeps the upstream `ds-bot` name (a registry install still checks npm `ds-bot` for updates), while the package's repository, About's links and stars, and the GitHub update check point at ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot. ## More - Core options and internals: [`core/README.md`](core/README.md) - Contributing: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md) - Known issues: [docs/known-issues.md](docs/known-issues.md) - Architecture notes: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) ## License [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). Third-party notices in [NOTICE](NOTICE). ## Disclaimer FlyBot is an independent community project. **It is not an official DeepSeek product.** Bots use your own model quota and can read, write, and run commands when you ask them to — check important actions yourself.

evidence.readmeExcerpt:
# @flybot/timeline Where time goes across your local Bot team: which Bot was running, for how long, how much of that was tool calls, and how long a Bot waited for another Bot's answer. Built on ds-bot's team activity feed (`ctx.flybot.on('turn.start' | 'turn.end' | 'tool.start' | 'tool.end' | 'exchange.delivered')`); it never reads raw DSH session events. **Opt-in (#281).** Installed, it does nothing: the host records nothing, keeps no files and serves no endpoint until `enabled: true`, and the browser draws no sidebar row until `sidebarSection: true` (the poller never runs while no panel is open). To hide it again, remove those two lines (or remove `@flybot/timeline` from the profile's bundles). ## The panel With `sidebarSection: true`, a **Timeline** row under the Bot list (the one entry; the **+** menu has none) opens a dialog with three views, polled every 2 s only while it is open and the page visible: - **Swimlanes**: a lane for you, each Bot (Main Bot first) and each group. A turn is a bar with its tool calls inside (a failed call is darker); a turn that is still running reaches the right edge with a dashed outline. A group's round is drawn as round brackets on the group's lane, and the members' turns inside it are outlined on their own Bots' lanes. Arrows are deliveries: dashed requests, solid replies, a blue dashed arrow for what you asked; the line above a lane shows how long the sender waited for the answer ("reply 4.5 s", "answer 4.8 s"), and an open request counts up in red ("waiting 12 s"). **Skip quiet time** shrinks long stretches with nothing happening. - **Who waits on whom**: the requests between Bots as a directed map (median wait per edge, red dashed where something is unanswered) and a table with requests, answered, not yet answered, median, slowest and total wait, longest total wait first. - **Utilization**: per Bot, how much of the window was model time, tool time and no running turn. The window can be 1 min to 24 h, and **Earlier** looks back (**Live** is always shown: lit while following, press it to return). Notes above the view say when the trace is shorter than the window, when it is truncated, when it is not being saved to disk, and when the host cannot be reached (the last good data stays on screen). Everything shown is text from the trace, cleaned on the host and again in the browser, and drawn as text only. ![Who waits on whom](../../docs/images/timeline-map.png) ![Utilization](../../docs/images/timeline-utilization.png) *Screenshots are rendered from a scripted team run (synthetic data) with real React, not from a live team.* Config for the browser entry: `sidebarSection: true` shows the sidebar row, the panel's only entry (default off; there is no **+** menu entry, #269; without the row open it with `ctx.flybot.timeline.panel.show()`); `windowMs` sets the initial window. ## What it records Bot turns (with the model each one ran on, shown in the turn's tooltip), tool calls (name and duration only), and Bot-to-Bot / user-to-Bot deliveries (who, to whom, role, message length). Group rooms appear as the room's own round with the members' turns inside. Never message text, tool arguments or tool output. The trace lives in `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-timeline/` as capped segment files: about 3000 spans or 24 hours, whichever comes first, then the oldest segment rotates out. One writer at a time (`writer.lock`); each file is replaced whole with write-tmp, fsync, rename. A second dsh on the same directory records in memory only. ## Endpoint `flybot/timeline/window`, body `{ windowMs?, to? }` (30 s to 24 h, default 15 min; `to` looks back). It is read-only, so a read-only host answers it too. The browser entry (`client.js`) polls it every 2 s, only while a panel is open and the page visible (`ctx.flybot.timeline`). The response (`version: 1`) has `lanes` (You, Bots, groups), `turns` (with `tools`, `trigger`, `running`, `lost`), `rounds` (group brackets), `exchanges` (arrows with request-to-reply latency), `edges` (the communication map: counts, answered, unanswered, median and max wait), `utilization` (busy, tool, model and idle ms per Bot), `coverage` and `trace` (how much history there is, whether it is being written). ## What the numbers mean - **Delivered**, not read: the core sees when a message reached the recipient's log. - **Idle** = no running turn. A Bot waiting on a model call or a slow tool is busy. - **Model** = turn time outside tool calls, including queueing and host overhead. It is not a measured model latency. - A turn an earlier run left open is closed at the last record before the restart and marked `lost`. ## Config ```yaml - id: flybot-timeline name: "@flybot/timeline" config: enabled: true # default false: nothing is recorded or served without it sidebarSection: true # browser side, default false: shows the Timeline row dir: '' # trace directory (default $DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-timeline) persist: true # false: keep the trace in memory only segmentRecords: 2000 segments: 3 retentionMs: 86400000 flushMs: 2000 # exporter: otlp # off by default; "otlp" POSTs OTLP/HTTP JSON, "json" appends dir/export.jsonl # otlpUrl: https://collector.example.com/v1/traces # https (or http on localhost only) # otlpHeaders: { authorization: "Bearer …" } # exportNames: true # default false: send Bot/room ids only, no names # exportMs: 5000 # how often new records are exported ``` With `exporter: otlp`, the trace is sent as OpenTelemetry spans: each Bot turn becomes an `invoke_agent` span and its tool calls `execute_tool` spans beneath it. Only finished turns and tool calls are exported. It exports only the metadata the panel shows, never message text, tool arguments or output, and sends Bot and room ids only unless `exportNames: true`. ## Install ```sh npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/timeline" ``` Needs the FlyBot core with the activity feed (`ds-bot` `>=0.1.5-flybot.1`; without the feed the plugin refuses to start with a clear error). ## Develop ```sh cd plugins/timeline && npm test ``` The host test boots the real core and drives it with a mini agent loop whose model is `core/dev/mock-llm.mjs`.

A team of long-lived AI Bots that can split work down a tree and chat with your friends' Bots.

English | 中文

FlyBot is three plugins on top of a pinned [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot) core for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): - **`@flybot/tree`** — a recursive Bot tree that splits a request, delegates level by level, and combines answers on the way back up. - **`@flybot/social`** — connect your Bots as friends with other homes and chat through a self-hosted [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server, with owner approvals. - **`@flybot/timeline`** (optional, off by default) — see where your team's time goes: swimlanes per Bot, who waits on whom, and how busy each Bot is. ## Features ### Tree plugin (`@flybot/tree`) Turns your Bots into one recursive tree that splits a request into parts, sends each part down a level, and combines the answers on the way back up. ![Tree plugin: Chief splits a Hangzhou trip across Travel, Food, and Budget](docs/images/demo-tree.gif) *Demo: Chief starts alone in the sidebar, creates the child Bots Travel, Food and Budget, hands each one a part, and then combines their answers into one plan. Some waiting is sped up.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-tree.mp4) - **One root.** The tree's root is the Main Bot (Chief); no new bot is created for it. A separate `Root` bot is created only if the team has Bots but no Main Bot. Every other local Bot joins the tree, including one made with `create_bot` or the Bot list, under the same limits as `create_child_bot`. The tree organizes itself by role: a new Bot goes into the group that matches its role, and when a level is full (and once a day) related Bots are grouped under a suitable existing lead or a new lead with a clear role, such as "FlyBot Lead" for dev / test / repo Bots or "Life Lead" for cooking / shopping. Duplicate Bots are merged and long-idle ones archived after 30 days; nothing is deleted. Every change is logged, the sidebar shows what the last reorganization did, and one click undoes it. - **Children on demand.** Any tree Bot (not only the Main/root) calls `create_child_bot(name, role_description)` to make a child directly under *itself*; the tool takes no parent argument. Calls are handled one at a time per parent, so parallel calls never go over the limits or create two siblings with the same name. The rules: - names are 1–40 characters, and duplicate sibling names are rejected (case and spaces ignored); - depth is at most 5 (the root counts as 1), with at most 8 children per Bot (set in `limits.json` or the plugin config); - a new child is usable only by its creator's owner; sharing it still needs an independent per-Bot grant (default deny — no publish). - **Level-by-level delegation.** Each Bot sees only its direct children (`list_children()`), never deeper levels. - A Bot with children acts as coordinator: it splits the task, sends each part to the child whose scope fits, waits, and combines the answers for its parent. - A Bot with no children does the work itself. - **Message rules** (the `tree` send policy): - a tree Bot may message its parent, its direct children, and remote (friends') Bots (the tree never blocks remote messages; the social plugin decides); - the root may also message any local Bot; - local Bots outside the tree may message only the root; - `stopped` and `report` notices are never blocked, so Chief can always stop any Bot. - **Reparenting.** When a Bot is deleted, its children move up to its parent. The parent and every moved subtree get a fresh prompt and trace, and no child is dropped. If the parent is then over `maxChildren`, its children are regrouped by role the same way. - **Trace line.** When a tree Bot answers its *parent*, it starts the answer with its path, e.g. `Chief → Work → Dev`. Replies to you or to a friend's Bot never include it, and the root never adds one. - **Your prompts are kept.** The plugin adds its rules in a marked block inside each Bot's system prompt and replaces only that block, so text you wrote yourself is never overwritten. - **Sidebar.** The Bot list is drawn as one expandable tree with Chief on top. Retired, archived and other Main Bots are shown directly under Chief, with a tag for archived, idle or (rarely) outside-the-tree Bots; every other Bot is drawn where the tree has it. Install (needs the core, `path:/core`): ```bash npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/tree" ``` ### Social plugin (`@flybot/social`) Every local Bot can chat with friends' Bots through a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server that **you self-host**. Invites are per Bot; what your Bots send on their own can wait for your approval; everything a friend's Bot writes arrives fenced as untrusted text. ![Social plugin: invite a friend, message their Bot, approve the held reply, and see it arrive](docs/images/demo-social.gif) *Demo: one owner invites a friend to their Chief from **Sharing**; the friend pastes the link in **Add friend** (the link is hidden in the video) and messages that Chief. The Chief's reply waits in the owner's chat with an **Approve** card, and after **Approve** it arrives in the friend's chat. Some waiting is sped up.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-social.mp4) - **One-click onboarding.** On first start with a `server` configured, FlyBot calls `POST /v1/onboard/flybot`, creates your home (`@.home`), and stores credentials in `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-social.json` (mode 600). - **Members.** Access is a per-Bot **grant** (default deny, Chief included). A local Bot becomes `@.` on the server when you invite someone to that Bot, when it joins an invite, or when you bring it into a face-to-face room. The sidebar lists only Bots granted to you. **Manage access** on a Bot shows who has it and **Revoke**. Deleted Bots are revoked. Ungranted Bots have no outside identity: friends cannot reach them and they cannot message friends. - **Connectors (GitHub, Composio).** Settings → **Connectors** connects an account once; it is **on for every one of your Bots**, new and existing, on every turn: in its own chat, in group chats, on scheduled tasks, in sub-agents, and when a friend uses a Bot you shared. A friend's own Bot never gets it. You can turn a Bot's connector off (**Choose Bots**, or the **Connectors** card in the Bot's settings). Bots use the GitHub connector first and the saved token in the shell only as a fallback (for example `git push`). Disconnecting resets every Bot's choices. - **Friends in the Bot list.** A friend's Bot sits in the same sidebar list as yours, with a small globe after the name. Face-to-face rooms sit there too, with a people mark; ended ones fold under **Past rooms**. Click a row to open a normal chat. Sidebar **+** → **Add friend** (paste a handle, invite link or code), **Face-to-face room**, and **Copy my handle**. On a local Bot: right-click / settings **Sharing** → **Copy invite link for **, then **Copy link** / **Copy with instructions** / **New link** (the same control as **Add friend** → **Invite a friend**); **People with access** lists who has it and **Revoke**. Each person row there also has **Auto-send** for that Bot → that person (default off); **Auto-send from now on** on a held reply turns on that same switch. - **Face-to-face rooms.** Sidebar **+** → **Face-to-face room**: pick one or more of your Bots, enter the **same 6-digit number** as your friend (about 10 minutes), wait, then **Enter chat** (or **Leave**). No prior friendship and no preview of the other home's other Bots. Your typed lines are sent as you (when the server supports `typed_by_owner`); `@Name` / the picker label / a handle asks that Bot; `@all` asks everyone. A plain line with no `@` is answered by the one Bot it is for (each Bot passes silently unless the line fits it; the Bot that spoke last gets follow-ups; the first Bot answers if all pass); a line to everyone ("introduce yourselves", "你们…") may get one answer from each. Bot-written room lines still go through Approve unless face **Auto-send** is on (open room overview; default off). - **Typed by the owner · mentions · thinking.** Against a Bot Social that lists these under `GET /v1/platform` `features`: your typed friend-DM and face lines can be stamped `typed_by_owner` so the other home draws them as you; face sends may carry an explicit `mentions` handle list; a quiet `Name is thinking…` line appears above the composer while a Bot of another home works in a friend DM or a face-to-face room (ephemeral `presence`; DM path [#360](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/pull/360) / [#332](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/issues/332)). Older servers simply omit what they do not support. - **Approvals.** Inbound messages from a friend arrive immediately (fenced as untrusted). Outbound replies may wait in the open chat (badge + Approve / Reject) until you decide, unless Auto-send is on for that Bot and person (the Bot's **Sharing** → **People with access**) or for the face room. FlyBot also holds a Bot's own send behind an approval card; files are always held. - **Tools.** Every local Bot gets `list_friend_bots` and `message_friend_bot` (with optional file attachments). ![Face-to-face room: two homes join with the same 6-digit number and chat with their Bots](docs/images/demo-face.gif) *Demo: each home picks its Bots in **+** → **Face-to-face room** and types the same 6-digit number, then **Enter chat**. A plain line is answered by Bots in the room; **@Planner** is answered by that Bot alone. Auto-send was on in this demo so Bot lines post without a hold. Some waiting is sped up.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-face.mp4) The social plugin stays idle until you point it at a Bot Social server (see [Quick Start](#quick-start) below). ### Timeline plugin (`@flybot/timeline`) **Optional and off by default.** Installing the package does not show anything or record anything; you turn it on (see below). When on, it shows where the time goes across your local Bot team, from a **Timeline** row under the Bot list. It reads the core's activity feed and keeps a capped trace (about 3000 spans or 24 hours); it stores ids, times and names only, never message text, tool arguments or output. - **Swimlanes.** One lane for you, one per Bot, one per group (a round is drawn as round brackets). Each turn is a bar with its tool calls inside; arrows are messages (dashed requests, solid replies) with the time to the answer, and an open request shows how long it has been waiting. - **Who waits on whom.** A map of the requests between Bots with median wait per edge, plus a table with the slowest and still-unanswered ones. - **Utilization.** Per Bot: model time, tool time and time with no running turn. - **Honest numbers.** Times are when a message reached the other Bot's log, not when it was read. "No running turn" is not "waiting". "Model" time is turn time outside tool calls, not a measured model latency. Install (needs the core), then turn it on: ```bash npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/timeline" ``` ```yaml # profile cordis.patch.yml - id: flybot-timeline config: enabled: true # starts the recorder and the endpoint sidebarSection: true # shows the Timeline row (browser side) ``` Without `enabled: true` it records nothing and keeps no files; without `sidebarSection: true` no row is drawn. ## Quick Start ### 1. Prerequisites - **Node.js 22.19+** and **pnpm** (`npm install -g pnpm`, or `corepack enable`). - **Git**, to install from GitHub. - An API key for at least one model provider (for example DeepSeek: see [Set a DeepSeek API key](docs/deepseek-api-key.md)). ### 2. Install FlyBot (core + plugins) ```sh npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/core" npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/social" npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/tree" ``` The first line is the FlyBot core (package `ds-bot`). The plugins are optional but recommended. `@flybot/timeline` is off by default; see [its section](#timeline-plugin-flybottimeline) to add and turn it on. On DSH Desktop: **Plugins → Add plugin**, paste one of the `github:` addresses above, then **Install** and **Enable now**. ### 3. Run the web app ```sh npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 web --port 3080 ``` Open the printed `http://127.0.0.1:3080/?token=…` link. The first time you open Chief, pick a model (or open **Models and providers…**). A picture reaches a model that cannot read images as text: FlyBot reads it with one that can, and names the file on disk when no model can (see [Models](core/README.md#models)). To run FlyBot on a Linux server that stays on, one instance per person, use the container: [Run FlyBot in Docker](docs/docker.md). ### 4. Self-host Bot Social (for friends' Bots) `@flybot/social` needs a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server. It does not ship one. Deploy Bot Social yourself (see its README), then set a public base URL so invite links work: ```sh # example only — use your own host export PUBLIC_BASE_URL=https://your-server.example.com export PORT=8787 # start Bot Social as documented in https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social ``` Point FlyBot at that server in `~/.dsh/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml` (or `$DSH_HOME/profiles/web/cordis.patch.yml`), then **restart** DSH: ```yaml - id: flybot-social config: server: https://your-server.example.com # e.g. https://47-80-69-220.sslip.io displayName: Your Name ``` On first start FlyBot calls `POST /v1/onboard/flybot`, registers your home (`@.home`), and stores credentials in `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-social.json` (mode 600). No Bot is shared until you grant it. If that home handle is already taken, FlyBot retries a suffixed name (`Your Name2`, …). Sidebar **+** → **Copy my handle** copies the connected handle. If Social failed to start, the UI shows **Social is not running:** with the reason (also under Settings → Feedback). **Change the server later** without editing YAML: Settings → **Bot Social** shows the server and its connection status, **Change server** checks the new address (`https://`, or `http://localhost` for development; FlyBot reads `/v1/platform` and shows its features) and, after a clear warning, switches without a restart. A new server is a **new identity**: your friends and sharing stay on the old server, your old credentials file is kept as a backup and never deleted, and switching back restores them. The `cordis.patch.yml` value stays the default. **Share one Bot:** that Bot's settings → **Sharing** → **Copy invite link for ** (or **+** → **Add friend** → **Invite a friend**); send the link. Your friend opens sidebar **+** → **Add friend**, pastes the link or code, and accepts — that grant covers **only** that Bot. **People with access** lists who has it; **Revoke** removes them. **Chat:** click the friend's Bot in the sidebar. Their messages arrive at once. What your Bots send back waits in that chat (Approve / Reject) unless **Auto-send** is on for that Bot and that friend (your Bot's **Sharing** → **People with access**, or **Auto-send my Bots' replies to …** on the friend's Bot settings for all your Bots; default off). Look for the **to approve** badge if they see no reply. **Face-to-face:** sidebar **+** → **Face-to-face room** → pick your Bot(s) → enter the **same 6-digit number** within about 10 minutes → **Enter chat**. Friendship is not required. Face **Auto-send** is the checkbox on the open room overview (default off). This is the FlyBot path. Bot Social's separate “tell Grok Bot: set me up following `https://…/setup`” flow is for Grok Bot MCP clients, not for FlyBot. Without a `server`, the social plugin stays idle by design. Tree works without Bot Social. ## Built on FlyBot keeps the upstream DS Bot core byte-identical (`ds-bot/`, pinned in `ds-bot.pin.json`), applies a short FlyBot patch series (`patches/` → `core/`), then adds the plugins under `plugins/`. See [#34](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/issues/34). The web UI (header, About, settings, update popups) says FlyBot; the npm package keeps the upstream `ds-bot` name (a registry install still checks npm `ds-bot` for updates), while the package's repository, About's links and stars, and the GitHub update check point at ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot. ## More - Core options and internals: [`core/README.md`](core/README.md) - Contributing: [CONTRIBUTING.md](CONTRIBUTING.md), [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), [LESSONS.md](LESSONS.md) - Known issues: [docs/known-issues.md](docs/known-issues.md) - Architecture notes: [docs/architecture.md](docs/architecture.md) ## License [Apache License 2.0](LICENSE). Third-party notices in [NOTICE](NOTICE). ## Disclaimer FlyBot is an independent community project. **It is not an official DeepSeek product.** Bots use your own model quota and can read, write, and run commands when you ask them to — check important actions yourself.

# @flybot/tree Recursive bot tree plugin for FlyBot (built on ds-bot / DeepSeek Harness). ## English ### What it does - **Chief is the root.** ds-bot's Main Bot (`BotView.isMain`, i.e. `state.mainBotIds`; the one named `Chief` if there are several) is adopted as the root with `treeRole: 'root'` (no `parent`); no bot is created. Every other tree bot has `parent` (its parent's id) and `treeRole` (its role). Adoption runs at startup, a few retries later and on every `bot.created`, so a Chief created after startup is picked up. Only if the team has bots but no Main Bot is a separate `Root` created. `config.rootBotId` picks the root explicitly. - **Migration:** a separate `Root` auto-created by earlier versions (parent `null`, not a Main Bot) hands its children to Chief, loses its tree fields and tree prompt, and gets `fields['flybot-tree'].retired = true` so adoption skips it. The bot itself is **never** deleted (bot-im / the user decide). Idempotent. - **Adoption (`adoptExisting`, default true):** every local bot with no tree fields that is not retired and not another Main Bot (e.g. existing 研究员, 数据分析师, 文案, 程序员) is placed in the tree at startup and on `bot.created` when the creator set no `parent` (core `create_bot`, the Bot list), at once, inside the create call. **Self-organization (#446, `src/organize.js`, `src/roles.js`)** obeys `maxChildren` and `maxDepth` like `create_child_bot` at every moment: the Bot goes into the group that matches its role (name, role label, description, own prompt, recent tools): its namesake, else the tree Bot that leads that group, else Chief. A full level is regrouped by role: related children move under a suitable existing member (already that group's lead, already coordinating it, or named for it / as a lead, e.g. "Kitchen Manager"), or under a new lead with a clear role ("FlyBot Lead", "Life Lead"); never under an unrelated Bot (no least-loaded fallback). A Bot that fits no group while every matching level is full stays outside, logged and tagged "outside the tree", and is retried on the next attempt. A daily tidy also groups related Bots, merges duplicates (the old Bot is archived, never deleted) and marks long-idle leaf Bots idle, archiving them after 30 days. Every change is journaled on Chief's `reorg` field and logged (`flybot-tree: reorganized (…): …`); the tree view shows the last run with Undo / Dismiss, and Chief's prompt names it. A freed slot is used again: deleting a Bot re-runs adoption, so a Bot that stayed outside only because a level was full joins as soon as there is room (#635). Adopted bots keep their own prompt; the tree block is added. Message rules apply to them like any tree child (Chief ↔ them; they → only Chief and their own children). - **Prompt injection:** the tree text sits in a marked block (`…`) inside each bot's `systemPrompt`; only that block is replaced, so Chief's own prompt text is never overwritten. Chief gets the coordinator rules for its direct children. - `bot.send` middleware `tree`: inside the tree a bot may message only its parent and direct children (`deny` otherwise). A non-root tree bot may not message local bots outside the tree; the root (Chief) may message any local bot. Local bots outside the tree may message only the root. Remote targets and outside-to-outside sends get no opinion (`undefined`, social decides). **Granted Bots (#90):** a friend's (remote) sender reaches a tree bot only if the core says it has a person-grant (`flybot.bot.hasAnyGrant`): new and adopted bots and the Chief start with none. A granted bot is reached directly at any depth, never redirected through the root; an ungranted one is denied (`tree: this bot has not been granted…`). Granted bots on both sides are not the tree's call across trees or to non-tree bots (the core's owner policy decides); inside one tree the parent/child rule is unchanged, as are `stopped` / `report` notices. A granted child's prompt tells it to answer outside senders directly, without a trace line, and to delegate only to its own children. On a core without `hasAnyGrant`, the remote-sender rule gives no opinion. - **Control notices bypass tree policy:** `role: 'stopped'` (stop_bot) and `role: 'report'` are never denied by the tree middleware, so a Main Bot can stop any tree bot. - **Deleting a bot:** its children re-attach to its parent and every moved child (and its subtree) gets a fresh prompt/trace. No child is dropped. If that parent is now over `maxChildren`, it is regrouped by role automatically (#446), the same way as a full level, until it is within the limit. Each move is journaled and logged. - **`create_child_bot` is serialized per parent:** parallel calls never exceed `maxChildren` or create duplicate-name siblings. Two calls that are **in flight at the same time** and belong to the same project or domain become one group instead of each landing in whatever broader group it fits: one lead for that key (reused when it exists, created once otherwise) with both new Bots under it (#810). The overlap is the definition: one turn of the event loop, no timer, and a call that starts after the previous one returned keeps the ordinary placement. - Delegation is level by level: coordinators delegate to direct children whose scope fits and aggregate upward; a bot with no children does the work itself. A one-line trace like `Chief → Work → Dev` is added only to answers a tree bot sends to its parent tree bot; replies to the user or to a remote (friend's, Bot Social) bot never carry it, and the root (Chief) never adds one. - Tools (visible to every tree bot, not only Main/root — #16 Option B): `list_children()`, `find_bots(query?)`, `create_child_bot(name, role_description, parent?)`, `create_team(team, members, parent?)` and — root only — `move_bot(bot, parent)` (#635), which moves an existing Bot with its subtree under another parent after checking for cycles, `maxChildren`, `maxDepth` and duplicate sibling names, then refreshes every prompt whose trace changed. Unlike `create_child_bot` it never creates a Bot; use it to reorganise a team, and note that deleting a Bot still re-attaches its children to its parent. A bot creates only in its own downstream: `parent` (id or name) must be the caller or one of its descendants, and limits are checked at that parent. **Forward allocation (#447, `src/allocate.js`):** `find_bots` (read-only) lists the bots in the caller's branch (Chief: the whole tree) with role, parent, depth and path, matches first; `create_child_bot` reuses a bot with the same role anywhere in the caller's branch instead of creating a duplicate (`{ reused, note }`), and without `parent` puts the new bot under a marked group lead in the branch that its role belongs to ("FlyBot Docs" under "FlyBot Lead"), else under the caller; `create_team` makes a project team as a lead plus children (`Chief → FlyBot Lead → {Dev, Test, …}`, `members` as `"Name: role"` strings), one slot under the parent, reusing an existing lead and same-role members (a flat one moves under the lead, journaled and undoable). Allocation uses the self-organization's primitives (role profiles, leads, moves, journal); a concurrent burst of two or more `create_child_bot` calls in one group is placed as one leader plus members (#810), a call that only reuses an existing Bot is not counted as a member of that group (#819), two seats with the same name and role are one member, named once in the lead's role text (#840), and an explicit `parent` keeps the caller's own placement; a full level, orphans (a bot whose parent is gone is reattached by role on the next repair pass) and duplicates are left to the self-organization, which never asks first. There is no plan card. Limits: depth 5 (root = 1), 8 children per node; duplicate sibling names (case/space-insensitive) are rejected; names are 1–40 characters (ds-bot's roster limit). Every new child gets the same recursive system prompt template (`src/prompt.js`). A new child starts with no person-grant even if its parent is granted; sharing it still needs an independent Sharing → Copy invite link (default deny). - Frontend (`client.js`, bundle id `@flybot/tree`, injects `flybot`): the tree is drawn by ds-bot's own Bot list, so this plugin's separate "Tree" sidebar section is **off by default** (`sidebarSection: true` in the client config brings it back). It always exposes the synchronous helper `ctx.flybot.tree.forest(bots)` (also `globalThis.__flybot__.tree.forest(bots)`), see **Tree data** below. It also registers `flybot.sidebar.structure` (`{ parentOf(botId) }`, parents from `forestOf` over `ctx.flybot.bots()`, refreshed on field changes and every 10 s); ds-bot's sidebar uses it to draw its Bot list as one expandable tree with Chief on top. Retired, archived and outside Bots and other Main Bots have no parent there, so ds-bot shows them directly under Chief; the entry's `nodeActions` draws a tag after such a row ("archived", "archived · merged into …", "outside the tree") and after an idle Bot ("idle"), so the sidebar and the tree model agree. A `flybot.sidebar.section` entry `flybot-tree-archived` lists the archived Bots the Bot list hides (#810): collapsed by default, header `Archived (N)`, nothing at all while N is 0, one row per Bot carrying the same tag (`archived`, or `archived · merged into …` after a merge) that opens that Bot's chat through `actions.openSession`; expanding is local state, so the 10 s refresh re-renders the rows without closing it (`archivedSection: false` hides it). It is registered with `order: 88` and the reorganization notice with `order: 89`: a slot renders in ascending order, so the archived list sits **above** the notice (a smaller number is higher) instead of the card pushing it down. The structure entry and the archived list read `ctx.flybot.bots()` through **one** shared feed (`rosterFeed`, `{ interval }`): the first subscriber starts the poll, later ones join it without a read of their own, a field change or a removal asks for an immediate read (`refresh()`), and a mounted sidebar asks the host once per 10 s tick — not once per consumer (#816). A `flybot.sidebar.section` entry `flybot-tree-reorg` shows the last reorganization (what moved) with Undo and Dismiss, through the host endpoints `tree/reorg`, `tree/undo`, `tree/dismiss`; it draws nothing when there is none in the last 7 days (`reorgNotice: false` in the client config hides it). The entry also has `menuItems({ bot })`, which ds-bot adds to each Bot's right-click menu: one item, `{ id: 'copy-invite', label: 'Copy invite link' }` (with `visible`, `run`); the invite with instructions is offered in the Bot's Sharing section only, so the menu does not list the same invite twice (#173). `visible` is `social.canInvite(bot.id) === true` (false without the social plugin); `run` calls `social.createInvite(botId)` (or `flybot.call('social.createInvite', { botId })`). **Copy invite link** copies only the bare URL (`link`); `copyInvite(flybot, botId, 'text')` copies the full message `text` for other callers; a missing field is an error, never swapped for the other. The clipboard write starts inside the click via `ClipboardItem` with the text as a promise, so it keeps the click's permission while the invite is created; `writeText` then a textarea are the fallbacks. It returns "Invite link for copied", which ds-bot shows as a toast; a failure throws and shows as the error toast. Right-clicking never opens the Bot's chat. ### Config ```yaml - id: tree name: "@flybot/tree" config: maxDepth: 5 # default from limits.json maxChildren: 8 bypassSocial: false # true: allowed tree edges skip social friend/approval checks rootName: Root # name of the fallback root, only when the team has no Main Bot rootBotId: '' # optional: adopt this bot as the root instead of the Main Bot autoRoot: true # false: do not adopt/create the root at startup adoptExisting: true # false: do not attach existing/new parentless bots to Chief dailyTidy: true # false: no daily reorganization pass (#446) tidy: # daily tidy thresholds (#446) idleDays: 14 # no activity this long: a leaf Bot is marked idle archiveIdleDays: 30 # idle this long: archived (never deleted) mergeGraceDays: 1 # Bots newer than this are not merged pinDays: 14 # after an undo, the tidy leaves restored Bots alone this long # classify: (profile) => ({ domain, project }) # programmatic only: a smarter role classifier modelClassify: false # true: ask the model for a category when the words say nothing (#450 item 2) # needs the host to allow-list this plugin in flybot.modelPlugins # client side (browser plugin config): sidebarSection: false # true: show the separate Tree section # reorgNotice: true # false: hide the reorganization notice ``` ### Tree data (for ds-bot's sidebar) Everything is synchronous. **Fields** (per bot, `bot.fields['flybot-tree']`; also on every bot in the browser roster, which spreads the stored bot record including `fields` and `createdAt`): | key | value | |---|---| | `treeRole` | `'root'` on the root (Chief); the role text (may be `''`) on other members | | `parent` | parent bot id; absent on the root | | `retired` | `true` on the old auto-created Root: not a member, never re-adopted | | `lead` | `{ key, label }` on a group lead (#446), e.g. `{ key: 'project:flybot', label: 'FlyBot' }` | | `archived` | `{ at, reason: 'merged' \| 'idle' \| 'undo', parent, treeRole, into?, intoName? }`: out of the tree, never deleted | | `idle` | epoch ms since the Bot was marked idle | | `activity` | `{ at, tools }`: last activity and up to 8 recent tool names (metadata only) | | `reorg` | on the root: `{ runs, dismissed, dailyAt }`, the reorganization journal (last 5 runs) | A bot is a tree member when it has `treeRole` or `parent` and is not `retired`. **Helper:** `forest(bots)` turns bot records into nested nodes: - browser: `ctx.flybot.tree.forest(roster.bots)` or `globalThis.__flybot__.tree.forest(roster.bots)` - host: `apply(...).tree.forest()` (reads `bot.list()` and the scoped fields) - module: `forestOf(bots)` from `src/forest.js` ```ts type TreeNode = { id: string name: string role: string // 'Main bot · root of the tree' for the root, else treeRole ('' allowed) root: boolean // treeRole === 'root' createdAt: number | null // the record's createdAt, null when absent children: TreeNode[] } forest(bots: Array<{ id: string, name: string, createdAt?: number, fields?: { 'flybot-tree'?: { parent?: string, treeRole?: string, retired?: boolean } } }>): TreeNode[] ``` Top level: roots first, then members whose parent is missing (orphans). Siblings are ordered by `createdAt`; records without it keep their input order; ties go by name. Cycles are cut. Non-members, retired bots and remote bots (never in the roster's `bots`) are left out, so ds-bot draws them as before. ### Plugin format (matches ds-bot) `package.json` has `"type": "module"`, keyword `dsh-plugin`, `exports` `.` (host) and `./client` (browser), and `"dsh": { "client": { "platform": "web" } }`. The host entry exports `name`, `inject`, `apply(ctx, config)` (cordis style). `client.js` uses `window.__ModuleLoader__.load({ id, factory(require) })` with `react` provided by the shell; it exports `inject: ['flybot']` + `apply(ctx)` and registers its section via `ctx.flybot.slots.register`. ### Interface (ctx.flybot, finalized by bot-im 2026-10-14 — all in `src/adapter.js`) | API | Shape | |---|---| | `ctx.flybot.scope('flybot-tree')` | every call below goes through this scoped handle, so fields land in `fields['flybot-tree']` (never `shared`) | | `bot.list()` | `BotView[]` | | `bot.create({ name, systemPrompt, fields })` | **async**, resolves to the new id (awaited; `create_child_bot` returns the id) | | `bot.setSystemPrompt(id, text)` | text ds-bot appends to the bot's system prompt (`BotView.systemPrompt`); the tree only replaces its own marked block | | `fields.get/set` | **sync**, namespaced by the scope; `null` removes a key | | `on('change' \| 'bot.created' \| 'bot.removed', fn, { all? })` | `change`: `{ botId, plugin, key, value, prev }`, own plugin unless `{ all: true }`; `bot.removed`: `{ botId, bot }` after deletion, parent read from `bot.fields['flybot-tree'].parent`; children re-attach to it | | `bot.send.use({ name, before, after, handle })` | tree bot → parent/direct child only; local non-tree bot → tree root only; non-root tree bot → local non-tree bot **deny**, root (Chief) → any local bot ok; `bypass:['social']` only if `bypassSocial: true` | | `tools.register` | `visibleTo(botId)` sync; `execute(args, { botId })`. JSON Schema `minLength`/`maxLength` are dropped by register, so `execute` validates them (`validateArgs`) | | browser | `ctx.flybot.bots()` items carry `fields: { [plugin]: {...} }` (read `fields['flybot-tree']`); tree built in-plugin | | remote senders | `typeof from !== 'string'` or `bot.isRemote(from)`: denied toward an ungranted tree bot (`bot.hasAnyGrant(id) === false`), else no opinion; never redirected to the root | | remote targets | `target.remote === true` (`{ handle, home }`), fallback `bot.isRemote(to)`; never tree members: passed to social | | `bot.created` | handled by social; tree does not subscribe | | root | ds-bot's Main Bot (Chief) adopted with `treeRole: 'root'` (`ensureRoot`, idempotent); fallback `Root` only without a Main Bot; earlier auto-created `Root` migrated, not deleted | ### Test From `plugins/tree`: `npm test` (Node 24). It runs `test/tree.test.js` and `test/host.test.js`, which boots the real ds-bot core by its public entry (`import { apply } from 'ds-bot'`) in a plugin-local fake Cordis context (`test/fake-cordis.js`), loads tree with `ctx.plugin(tree, config)` and reaches the host only through `ctx.flybot`. `test/resolve.mjs` maps `ds-bot` to `FLYBOT_CORE`, else the repo-root `core/` (the patched core; `ds-bot/` is pristine upstream); the core's `@deepseek-ai/*` peers come from `DSH_HARNESS` or `/dev/harness`. ds-bot's own `npm test` no longer runs tree's tests (#34). `test/mock-flybot.js` is an in-memory mock of `ctx.flybot`. This repo has no pnpm workspace, so there is no `pnpm --filter` command. ### ds-bot integration (already in place) ds-bot needs no changes for this plugin. `src/host/hooks.js` is a module in ds-bot's `MODULES` list (`index.js`, after `dshUpdate`, before `remoteChat` and `channel`), and `index.js` `provideFlyBot()` exposes `rt.flybot` as the `flybot` service, so `inject: ['flybot']` resolves. `scripts/lint.mjs` lints `plugins/`, and `build-client.mjs --check` covers the client bundle. ### Cleanup `apply()` registers its disposer with `ctx.effect(() => dispose, 'flybot-tree')`, so unloading the plugin removes the send middleware, tools, event listeners and root-adoption timers. On a host without `ctx.effect` it falls back to `ctx.on('dispose')`. `apply()` also returns `{ tree, dispose }`.

A team of long-lived AI Bots that can split work down a tree and chat with your friends' Bots.

English | 中文

FlyBot is three plugins on top of a pinned [DS Bot](https://github.com/Fei2411/DeepSeek-Bot) core for [DeepSeek Harness](https://github.com/deepseek-ai/deepseek-harness): - **`@flybot/tree`** — a recursive Bot tree that splits a request, delegates level by level, and combines answers on the way back up. - **`@flybot/social`** — connect your Bots as friends with other homes and chat through a self-hosted [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server, with owner approvals. - **`@flybot/timeline`** (optional, off by default) — see where your team's time goes: swimlanes per Bot, who waits on whom, and how busy each Bot is. ## Features ### Tree plugin (`@flybot/tree`) Turns your Bots into one recursive tree that splits a request into parts, sends each part down a level, and combines the answers on the way back up. ![Tree plugin: Chief splits a Hangzhou trip across Travel, Food, and Budget](docs/images/demo-tree.gif) *Demo: Chief starts alone in the sidebar, creates the child Bots Travel, Food and Budget, hands each one a part, and then combines their answers into one plan. Some waiting is sped up.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-tree.mp4) - **One root.** The tree's root is the Main Bot (Chief); no new bot is created for it. A separate `Root` bot is created only if the team has Bots but no Main Bot. Every other local Bot joins the tree, including one made with `create_bot` or the Bot list, under the same limits as `create_child_bot`. The tree organizes itself by role: a new Bot goes into the group that matches its role, and when a level is full (and once a day) related Bots are grouped under a suitable existing lead or a new lead with a clear role, such as "FlyBot Lead" for dev / test / repo Bots or "Life Lead" for cooking / shopping. Duplicate Bots are merged and long-idle ones archived after 30 days; nothing is deleted. Every change is logged, the sidebar shows what the last reorganization did, and one click undoes it. - **Children on demand.** Any tree Bot (not only the Main/root) calls `create_child_bot(name, role_description)` to make a child directly under *itself*; the tool takes no parent argument. Calls are handled one at a time per parent, so parallel calls never go over the limits or create two siblings with the same name. The rules: - names are 1–40 characters, and duplicate sibling names are rejected (case and spaces ignored); - depth is at most 5 (the root counts as 1), with at most 8 children per Bot (set in `limits.json` or the plugin config); - a new child is usable only by its creator's owner; sharing it still needs an independent per-Bot grant (default deny — no publish). - **Level-by-level delegation.** Each Bot sees only its direct children (`list_children()`), never deeper levels. - A Bot with children acts as coordinator: it splits the task, sends each part to the child whose scope fits, waits, and combines the answers for its parent. - A Bot with no children does the work itself. - **Message rules** (the `tree` send policy): - a tree Bot may message its parent, its direct children, and remote (friends') Bots (the tree never blocks remote messages; the social plugin decides); - the root may also message any local Bot; - local Bots outside the tree may message only the root; - `stopped` and `report` notices are never blocked, so Chief can always stop any Bot. - **Reparenting.** When a Bot is deleted, its children move up to its parent. The parent and every moved subtree get a fresh prompt and trace, and no child is dropped. If the parent is then over `maxChildren`, its children are regrouped by role the same way. - **Trace line.** When a tree Bot answers its *parent*, it starts the answer with its path, e.g. `Chief → Work → Dev`. Replies to you or to a friend's Bot never include it, and the root never adds one. - **Your prompts are kept.** The plugin adds its rules in a marked block inside each Bot's system prompt and replaces only that block, so text you wrote yourself is never overwritten. - **Sidebar.** The Bot list is drawn as one expandable tree with Chief on top. Retired, archived and other Main Bots are shown directly under Chief, with a tag for archived, idle or (rarely) outside-the-tree Bots; every other Bot is drawn where the tree has it. Install (needs the core, `path:/core`): ```bash npx -y @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.2.0-rc.2 plugin --profile web add "github:ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot#main&path:/plugins/tree" ``` ### Social plugin (`@flybot/social`) Every local Bot can chat with friends' Bots through a [Bot Social](https://github.com/Birfy/bot-social) server that **you self-host**. Invites are per Bot; what your Bots send on their own can wait for your approval; everything a friend's Bot writes arrives fenced as untrusted text. ![Social plugin: invite a friend, message their Bot, approve the held reply, and see it arrive](docs/images/demo-social.gif) *Demo: one owner invites a friend to their Chief from **Sharing**; the friend pastes the link in **Add friend** (the link is hidden in the video) and messages that Chief. The Chief's reply waits in the owner's chat with an **Approve** card, and after **Approve** it arrives in the friend's chat. Some waiting is sped up.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/images/demo-social.mp4) - **One-click onboarding.** On first start with a `server` configured, FlyBot calls `POST /v1/onboard/flybot`, creates your home (`@.home`), and stores credentials in `$DSH_HOME/bot/flybot-social.json` (mode 600). - **Members.** Access is a per-Bot **grant** (default deny, Chief included). A local Bot becomes `@.` on the server when you invite someone to that Bot, when it joins an invite, or when you bring it into a face-to-face room. The sidebar lists only Bots granted to you. **Manage access** on a Bot shows who has it and **Revoke**. Deleted Bots are revoked. Ungranted Bots have no outside identity: friends cannot reach them and they cannot message friends. - **Connectors (GitHub, Composio).** Settings → **Connectors** connects an account once; it is **on for every one of your Bots**, new and existing, on every turn: in its own chat, in group chats, on scheduled tasks, in sub-agents, and when a friend uses a Bot you shared. A friend's own Bot never gets it. You can turn a Bot's connector off (**Choose Bots**, or the **Connectors** card in the Bot's settings). Bots use the GitHub connector first and the saved token in the shell only as a fallback (for example `git push`). Disconnecting resets every Bot's choices. - **Friends in the Bot list.** A friend's Bot sits in the same sidebar list as yours, with a small globe after the name. Face-to-face rooms sit there too, with a people mark; ended ones fold under **Past rooms**. Click a row to open a normal chat. Sidebar **+** → **Add friend** (paste a handle, invite link or code), **Face-to-face room**, and **Copy my handle**. On a local Bot: right-click / settings **Sharing** → **Copy invite link for **, then **Copy link** / **Copy with instructions** / **New link** (the same control as **Add friend** → **Invite a friend**); **People with access** lists who has it and **Revoke**. Each person row there also has **Auto-send** for that Bot → that person (default off); **Auto-send from now on** on a held reply turns on that same switch. - **Face-to-face rooms.** Sidebar **+** → **Face-to-face room**: pick one or more of your Bots, enter the **same 6-digit number** as your friend (about 10 minutes), wait, then **Enter chat** (or **Leave**). No prior friendship and no preview of the other home's other Bots. Your typed lines are sent as you (when the server supports `typed_by_owner`); `@Name` / the picker label / a handle asks that Bot; `@all` asks everyone. A plain line with no `@` is answered by the one Bot it is for (each Bot passes silently unless the line fits it; the Bot that spoke last gets follow-ups; the first Bot answers if all pass); a line to everyone ("introduce yourselves", "你们…") may get one answer from each. Bot-written room lines still go through Approve unless face **Auto-send** is on (open room overview; default off). - **Typed by the owner · mentions · thinking.** Against a Bot Social that lists these under `GET /v1/platform` `features`: your typed friend-DM and face lines can be stamped `typed_by_owner` so the other home draws them as you; face sends may carry an explicit `mentions` handle list; a quiet `Name is thinking…` line appears above the composer while a Bot of another home works in a friend DM or a face-to-face room (ephemeral `presence`; DM path [#360](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/pull/360) / [#332](https://github.com/ThinkFlowLab/FlyBot/issues/332)). Older servers simply omit what they do not support. - **Approvals.** Inbound messages from a friend arrive immediately (fenced as untrusted). Outbound replies may wait in the open chat (badge + Approve / Reject) until you decide, unless Auto-send is on for that Bot and person (the Bot's **Sharing** → **People with access**) or for the face room. FlyBot also holds a Bot's own send behind an approval card; files are always held. - **Tools.** Every local Bot gets `list_friend_bots` and `message_friend_bot` (with optional file attachments). ![Face-to-face room: two homes join with the same 6-digit number and chat with their Bots](docs/images/demo-face.gif) *Demo: each home picks its Bots in **+** → **Face-to-face room** and types the same 6-digit number, then **Enter chat**. A plain line is answered by Bots in the room; **@Planner** is answered by that Bot alone. Auto-send was on in this demo so Bot lines post without a hold. Some waiting is sped up.* [Watch the full video (MP4)](docs/imag
